text: Confidential Mafia is social deduction played on Base, where the chain itself cannot spoil the secret.
Mafia only works if nobody knows who the Mafia is. On a public blockchain, that's the hard part. Every transaction is visible, so a naive on-chain Mafia leaks the whole game.
We solve that with Inco Lightning. Players join a lobby with their wallet, and roles are dealt as encrypted values that live on Inco.
Each player can decrypt exactly one thing: their own role. Inco's per-handle access control enforces it, so no server, no operator, and no other player can read it.
Here the app fetches this player's encrypted role handle from the contract, and runs an attested decrypt signed by the player's own key. The role appears only in this browser.
Now the core idea. At night, every living player sends the exact same transaction: submit night action, with a target.
Nothing on chain distinguishes a Mafia kill from a Doctor save from a Villager doing nothing at all. The contract works it out entirely under encryption.
It compares the encrypted role against the Mafia and Doctor thresholds, then uses encrypted select to add a kill weight, or to raise a protection flag. No branch ever reveals which one happened.
Resolution folds every target with an encrypted running maximum, and computes whether the victim dies, accounting for the Doctor's protection, still fully encrypted.

Only two values are ever revealed per night: which player was hit, and whether anyone actually died. Those come back as a covalidator-signed attestation, verified on chain before the contract will accept them.
A player's role becomes public only when they die. Everyone still alive stays encrypted, which is what lets the game decide a winner without exposing the survivors.
By day, voting is deliberately public, because arguing about a visible vote is the fun part. The night is what has to stay secret.
A Gemini narrator posts the story to the Telegram group between phases. It receives a public-events-only type, so it is structurally incapable of leaking a role it was never given.

Gemini also plays. These are real AI players with their own wallets, and they run under the same constraint as humans: each can decrypt only its own role, and reasons about everyone else from public state alone.
That means a game can start even without a full lobby, and the AI is never privileged over you.
Everything you just saw is live on Base Sepolia, in a Telegram Mini App, with real Inco attestations. Hidden roles, hidden night actions, and an AI that doesn't know the answer either.
